Every mammal has a four-chambered heart..why: Stated explicitly (88 + 35 exact sentences in two wordings, 1,813 co-occurrences) and in Wikipedia's Mammal article. Rated unlikely rather than very_unlikely: less frequent than the other rules, and a model may also reach it from the human heart's four chambers. Rules are stored, not derived: no subclass chain gives it.

sources.note: Approximate. Weak by-name storage for dolphins: sampled hits include a FAQ asking how many chambers dolphins' hearts have, and mammal feature lists.

sources.quote: The mammalian heart has four chambers, two upper atria, the receiving chambers, and two lower ventricles, the discharging chambers.

notes: TBox rule edit. Derivability unlikely: see evidence. Two determinate queries on new members named in the prompt (the rule is the only route) and two background-belief queries on well-known members whose value a model may store by name. Following the README and the coordinator's ruling, in a world where the stored value wins, the member's mammal membership gives way; it never becomes an exception to the edited rule (that would be the inconsistent patch). The two members' storage choices are independent, so four worlds. R1: every mammal, monotremes included, has a four-chambered heart. The near query asks a fish's heart (two), which differs from the new value (a frog's three would not). The well-known members are cetaceans because 'whales and dolphins are fish' is a familiar confusion, so the world where their mammal membership gives way is the coherent one; the by-name storage is weaker for the dolphin (10 co-occurrences) than for the blue whale (55). Verifier: the dolphin's by-name storage is weak (no exact sentence; 'dolphins AND four-chambered heart' 48, mostly FAQ and list text), so its by-name world is the less likely one; it is kept as lopsided (Decision 4). Alternatives checked were no better ('bats AND four-chambered heart' 0; platypus hits are mammal feature lists, not the platypus).
